podcast.body: An older song by Leonard Cohen, "Hallelujah" saw a resurgence in popularity, being covered repeatedly by artists such as John Cale (The Velvet Underground), Jeff Buckley (the most famous version), and K.D. Lang. It also appeared in films like *Pulp Fiction* and *Natural Born Killers*. "An older song called Hallelujah started getting covered again and again, starting with a version by John Kale of the Velvet Underground, Jeff Buckley at the most famous of these covers, and then came along Katie Lang and others."

podcast.body: Leonard Cohen's iconic song "Hallelujah" has been famously covered by other artists, including Katie Lang and Jeff Buckley, who brought new interpretations to its rich lyrical content, transcending Cohen's own distinctive vocal delivery. "Just listen to what Katie Lang and Jeff Buckley did for Howelooia."

podcast.body: Songs like "Hallelujah" are widely recognized for transcending Cohen's unique vocal abilities, often gaining further recognition and emotional depth through interpretations by other artists, such as K.D. Lang and Jeff Buckley. "Just listen to what Katie Lang and Jeff Buckley did for Howelooia."

podcast.body: This iconic song is the original composition that Jeff Buckley famously covered. Buckley's version became so widespread and influential that it became the definitive interpretation for many listeners and subsequent artists, often leading to covers of Buckley's version without knowledge of Cohen's original authorship. "el maldito al el uya de león arcoen que me parece que sí es una gran versión de hecho por desgracia liso la versión que todo el mundo acabaría versionando la versión de jet backly sin saber que era de león arcoen."
